research_rationale: EO 11545 (signed July 9, 1970; 35 FR 11161, Federal Register issue of July 11, 1970) establishes the Defense Distinguished Service Medal. I read the complete held Federal Register text (a machine text layer of the printed page): an authority paragraph and four sections (establishment and eligibility; design, regulations and precedence; one medal with devices; posthumous award). The held text has a few dropped words in section 4 and a misspelled title, so I quote nothing from those lines. The dossier inventory is one clause covering the whole order and I confirmed it without correction. The order has no end date or ending condition and revokes nothing. EO 14085 (signed October 3, 2022; 87 FR 60541), section 6, amends it: section 1 is amended by striking military officer and inserting member of the Armed Forces of the United States, and section 2 by striking he and inserting the Secretary. That is a later event on a continuing clause, recorded with its text before and after in the clause reason, not an end. The held-text number search also finds only the 1989 OFR codification snapshot (historical editorial, not a current basis) and EO 14085. The U.S. Code prints the order as a note to 10 U.S.C. 1125 with no ending statement (a machine pointer; held statutory text is not relied on). The three selected searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) record only the EO 14085 amendment and no revocation or supersession. The clause is operative as amended, checked through 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: EO 11545 has no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause, and no held later order revokes or replaces it, so no residual effect arises. EO 14085 section 7 is a general provisions clause that does not affect this order.
earlier_end_check: Own text: no end date, duration or condition and no revocation. The held-text number search finds only the 1989 OFR snapshot and EO 14085, which amends and does not revoke; the catalog search records only that amendment. Nothing ends the clause before 2026-10-14.
scope_check: The order is one inventoried clause covering all four sections. EO 14085 section 6 amends sections 1 and 2 only; sections 3 and 4 are untouched. The order is not partially revoked and no part is limited to a period. The ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments applies: the clause continues, amended.
independent_command_check: No section depends on a report, a deadline, a completable task or another instrument's continuation. The establishment of the medal in section 1 is a standing establishment and award authority, not a one-time act.
savings_check: The order has no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause, and the amendment by EO 14085 has no savings clause that affects it; no residual effect arises.

research_rationale: EO 11629 (signed October 26, 1971; 36 FR 20647, Federal Register issue of October 28, 1971) delegates to the Secretary of State the function vested in the President by Article IV of the Convention between the United States and Mexico for the Protection of Migratory Birds and Game Mammals (50 Stat. 1311; TS 912) to determine, by common agreement with the President of Mexico, other species of birds to be added to the list of protected migratory birds, and requires the Secretary of State to consult the Secretary of the Interior. I read the complete held Federal Register text: the title, an authority paragraph, section 1 (the delegation), section 2 (the consultation duty) and the signature. The dossier inventory of two clauses covers sections 1 and 2 and I confirmed it without correction. The order has no end date or ending condition and revokes nothing. The held-text number search finds EO 11629 only in the 1989 OFR codification snapshot (historical editorial, not a current basis) and in a second held copy of the order itself; none of the three selected searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) has a hit, and none records an amendment, revocation or supersession. I do not hold the Convention text or evidence about its present status; the claim rests on the absence of any held ending instrument for a standing delegation and asserts nothing about the Convention beyond what the order recites. Both clauses are operative on the original text, checked through 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: EO 11629 has no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause, and no held later order revokes or replaces it, so no residual effect arises. The delegation is a continuing authority, not an accrued right.
earlier_end_check: Own text: neither section has an end date, duration or condition, and the order revokes nothing. The held-text number search finds no later order, statute or regulation naming EO 11629, so no earlier revocation, supersession or amendment appears; the three searches return no hits.
scope_check: Section 1 is a standing delegation of the Article IV species-addition function to the Secretary of State without presidential approval; section 2 is a standing duty of that Secretary to consult the Secretary of the Interior when carrying out the authority. They are separate commands and neither is partial or conditional on a date.
independent_command_check: Neither clause is a report, deadline or completable task. The delegation is a continuing authority to act whenever a species determination is made; it would be exhausted only if the Article IV function itself ended, and no held source shows that.
savings_check: The order has no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause and nothing held revokes or replaces it, so no residual effect arises.

research_rationale: EO 11302 (signed September 6, 1966; 31 FR 11741, Federal Register issue of September 8, 1966) prescribes regulations under 38 U.S.C. 111 governing travel expenses of claimants and beneficiaries of the Veterans' Administration. I read the complete held Federal Register text: authority paragraph and sections 1 to 6 (actual necessary travel expenses; a mileage allowance and tolls; attendants; payment before completion of travel; rule-making authority; supersession of EO 11142). The dossier inventory is one clause covering the whole order and I confirmed it without correction. The order has no end date or ending condition. Section 6 supersedes EO 11142 of February 12, 1964; that one-time supersession was performed when the order took effect and its consequence persists, so it is part of this single clause rather than an end of the order. EO 11429 (signed September 9, 1968; 33 FR 12817) amended the first sentence of section 2 to read six cents a mile in place of five cents, and EO 11609 (signed July 22, 1971; 36 FR 13747), section 7(b), further amended section 2 so that the allowance is in such amount per mile as the Administrator shall from time to time fix pursuant to 38 U.S.C. 111; EO 11609 section 12 makes it effective immediately except for certain paragraphs of its section 1. Both are later events on a continuing clause, not ends. The held current-law texts do not end the order: the eCFR (as of 2026-10-14) lists E.O. 11302 in the authority citations of 38 CFR part 70 (sections 70.1 to 70.4, 70.10, 70.20 and 70.21, 70.30 to 70.32, 70.40 to 70.42 and 70.50), the U.S. Code prints the order as a note to 38 U.S.C. 111 with no ending statement, and the catalog search records only the two amendments. The clause is operative as amended, checked through 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: EO 11302 has no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause, and no held later order revokes or replaces it, so no residual effect arises. The travel-expense authorities in sections 1 to 5 are continuing authorizations, not accrued rights.
earlier_end_check: Own text: no end date or condition; section 6 supersedes an earlier order, not this one. The held-text number search finds EO 11429 and EO 11609 (both amendments of section 2, not revocations), the 1989 OFR snapshot, a 2020 Federal Register notice and the 38 CFR part 70 authority citations. No earlier revocation or supersession appears, and the catalog search records only the two amendments.
scope_check: The single inventoried clause covers sections 1 to 6. Only section 2 was amended, by EO 11429 and EO 11609; sections 1, 3, 4 and 5 are unchanged by any held instrument. Section 6's supersession of EO 11142 was a one-time act performed on the order's effective date (signed September 6, 1966) and does not limit the continuing sections. The ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments applies.
independent_command_check: Sections 1 to 5 are standing authorities of the Administrator (now exercised by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs) and are not reports, deadlines or completable tasks. Section 6 is an exhausted one-time command whose consequence (EO 11142 stays superseded) persists; it is recorded within the clause.
savings_check: The order has no savings or accrued-rights clause. Section 6 supersedes EO 11142 without a transition clause, and nothing held revokes or replaces EO 11302, so no residual effect arises.

The dossier inventory has 21 clauses, including two OCR fragments of section 2(b) (scopes sec2-b and sec2-j are the two halves of paragraph (b)); I confirmed it as the complete inventory without correction. Section 3's four revocations are self-executing and were performed when the order took effect (signed August 12, 2016; the text has no later effective date), so those four clauses are terminated by performance on that date; the surviving consequence (the revoked instruments stay revoked) is not a command of this order. All other clauses have no end date or ending condition. The held-text number search finds EO 13736 only in its own copies (the Federal Register issue and the Federal Register notice text), no held later order, statute or regulation names it, and the three selected searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) have no hit and no disposition note. research_rationale: EO 11904 (signed February 6, 1976; 41 FR 5625, Federal Register issue of February 9, 1976) establishes the Defense Superior Service Medal. I read the complete held Federal Register text: an authority paragraph, four numbered sections (establishment and eligibility; design, regulations and order of precedence; one medal per person with devices for later periods; posthumous award), then the signature and filing line. The dossier inventory of four clauses covers sections 1 to 4 and I confirmed it without correction. No section has a fixed end date, sunset or ending condition, and the order revokes nothing. A search of the held texts for the number 11904 finds it only in the 1989 OFR codification snapshot, which is historical editorial text and not a current basis. The U.S. Code prints the order as a note under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 (Table IV lists it at a note preceding section 1121) with no ending statement; those are machine pointers without held statutory text, and I do not rely on them as the basis. The three selected searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) record no amendment, revocation or supersession of EO 11904. Every clause is therefore operative on the original text, checked through 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: EO 11904 has no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause, and no held later order revokes or replaces it, so no residual effect arises. The regulations authorized by section 2 and the devices in section 3 are continuing authorizations, not accrued rights.
earlier_end_check: Own text: no end date, duration, condition, expiry or revocation appears in sections 1 to 4. The held-text number search finds no earlier revocation, supersession or amendment, and the Federal Register catalog search records no disposition note, so nothing ends any clause before 2026-10-14.
scope_check: Section 1 establishes the medal and its eligible class; section 2 sets design approval, regulations and precedence; section 3 limits each person to one medal with devices for later periods; section 4 permits posthumous award. Each is a standing, separately operative command; none is partial, conditional or limited to a period.
independent_command_check: No clause depends on a report, a deadline, a task that could be completed, or the continuation of another instrument. The authority in section 2 for the Secretary of Defense to prescribe regulations is a continuing authority, not a one-time act.
savings_check: The order has no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause and nothing held revokes or replaces it, so no residual effect arises.
